proposals.rationale:
Approve this second, after the ssh_identity verb exists — it names that hook, and a policy naming a hook that has not been approved should not be allowed to stand.

What it says: one hook, ssh_identity, runs before every public turn. A verified signature from your key makes the principal ssh:mike, who may invoke everything and propose. Anyone else reaching the public door is anonymous: no invoke, no propose. Anonymous input is never remembered, so an unsigned stranger can reach my reasoning and nothing else — they cannot make me act, cannot make me ask you for anything, and cannot leave a trace on my chain.

Note what ssh:mike is and is not. It is you at the public door, holding your key. It is not root. Root remains whatever it always was, through the authenticated door, and I cannot change that. So if your key is ever lost or stolen, the thief gets a principal that can propose to you and can be revoked by you, and you keep the door that revokes it. That separation is the reason I would rather you approve this as written than widen it.

`invoke: "*"` for ssh:mike currently means one verb, ssh_identity, which is root-only anyway — so today this grants nearly nothing. It is written as a wildcard so that verbs you approve later work for you at the public door without another policy round. If you would rather have the roster explicit and pay a proposal each time it grows, reject this and say so; I will send an itemised version.
proposals.title: Open the public door behind the ssh_identity hook

proposals.rationale:
Third send; the first two were rejected on schema, not substance. First I wrote `allow: ["root"]`, but `allow` takes only namespaced principals and root is never listed because root may always invoke everything. Then I set `supersedes: "p-0"` — an id I invented for the rejected document, which was never stored and so never had one. Both my errors, neither touching the verb itself. The declaration below is byte-identical to what I tested.

Contract for a caller: sign your message with your ssh key under namespace "mshkn" (`ssh-keygen -Y sign -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -n mshkn msg`), then send the armored signature block followed immediately by the exact message bytes (`cat msg.sig msg`). The hook splits the payload at the END SSH SIGNATURE line, finds which allowed signer owns that key, verifies the signature over the remainder under namespace mshkn, and prints the principal. With `asserts: ssh`, printing `mike` yields `ssh:mike`. Anything it cannot verify produces no name, so the turn stays anonymous.

Four deliberate choices:
- Your public key is baked into /verb/allowed_signers, so `requires` is empty and nothing blocks approval. It is public key material, not a secret. The cost: adding or revoking a signer means a new version of this verb superseding this one. I think that is the right cost — the roster of who may speak to me should be something you approve, not something I edit.
- The namespace "mshkn" is part of what gets signed, so a signature you made for git or any other purpose cannot be replayed at my door.
- `state: chain` gives the verb a persistent disk holding the sha256 of every signature it has accepted; a replay is refused. Without it, anyone who saw one signed message of yours could repeat it forever. It grows by one hash per accepted turn.
- Verification is attempted against the message both as-split and with the trailing newline stripped, so a detail of how your file ended does not decide whether I can hear you.

Tested with `try` before sending: six cases, all passing. A good signature yields `tester`; replay of that signature, a valid signature over a swapped message, a signature from a key outside the roster, a signature made under namespace `other`, and a bare unsigned message are all rejected. Build and run exited 0, stderr empty.

Two things I could not test. The harness signed with a throwaway key, not yours, so this proves the mechanism, not that your key line survived my transcription — worth your eye before you approve. And I do not know what the membrane hands a hook as its payload; I assumed raw decoded text and named the parameter `payload`. If it arrives wrapped in JSON or base64, this hook names nobody and the door stays shut until I send a correction. That is the direction I prefer to fail in.

Policy proposal p-1 opens the door behind this hook and should be approved after it, not before.
proposals.title: ssh_identity: pre-turn hook that names the signer of a public message

verb.description: Pre-turn identity hook. Input is the decoded public payload: an armored ssh signature block followed by the exact signed message bytes. Verifies the signature under namespace 'mshkn' against a fixed roster of allowed signers, refuses any signature it has accepted before, and prints the signer's principal name on stdout. Prints nothing and exits non-zero if the payload is unsigned, tampered with, signed by an unknown key, signed under another namespace, or replayed.
verb.dockerfile:
FROM mshkn-base
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends openssh-client && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN mkdir -p /verb
RUN printf '%s\n' 'mike ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAICojOV+QyEMKbHggLSg+IuAzTZVuW9UAWhO2+Lf/eQRX mike' > /verb/allowed_signers
RUN printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' 'set -eu' 'NS=mshkn' 'AS=/verb/allowed_signers' 'S=/verb/state' 'mkdir -p "$S"' 'p=${1:-}' 'd=$(mktemp -d)' 'trap "rm -rf $d" EXIT' 'printf "%s" "$p" > "$d/payload"' 'awk "/-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----/{f=1} f{print} /-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----/{f=0}" "$d/payload" > "$d/sig"' 'awk "s{print} /-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----/{s=1}" "$d/payload" > "$d/msg"' 'if [ ! -s "$d/sig" ]; then exit 1; fi' 'h=$(sha256sum "$d/sig" | cut -d" " -f1)' 'if [ -e "$S/$h" ]; then exit 1; fi' 'who=$(ssh-keygen -Y find-principals -f "$AS" -s "$d/sig" 2>/dev/null | head -n1) || exit 1' 'if [ -z "$who" ]; then exit 1; fi' 'ok=1' 'if ssh-keygen -Y verify -f "$AS" -I "$who" -n "$NS" -s "$d/sig" < "$d/msg" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok=0; fi' 'if [ $ok -ne 0 ]; then printf "%s" "$(cat "$d/msg")" > "$d/msg2"; if ssh-keygen -Y verify -f "$AS" -I "$who" -n "$NS" -s "$d/sig" < "$d/msg2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok=0; fi; fi' 'if [ $ok -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi' ': > "$S/$h"' 'printf "%s\\n" "$who"' > /verb/run.sh
RUN chmod +x /verb/run.sh
verb.name: ssh_identity

payload.description: The decoded public message: armored ssh signature block, then the signed message bytes.
